messages:
sam: @here seeing a spike in GPU attach fails in us-east1, started ~15:42 UTC. prob with local NVMe writeback — hosts reporting I/O errors and cleaner jobs stuck.
ops-bot: Alert: nvme_io_errors on host gnode-8342 (err rate ~0.6%).
kai: digging in — quick grep shows ephemeral-cleaner waiting on metadata RPCs; NFS/metadata timeouts cause cleaner to block. when cleaner blocks it holds tempfiles and writeback stalls -> iops congestion.
maria: if janitor threads block they stop deleting tempfiles and disk fills, which then breaks GPU attach. do we have a metric for tempfile backlog? https://grafana.redwood/board/ephemeral
sam: grafana shows tempfile_count up x4 in 12m and scratch disk_used% hitting 92% on affected hosts.
kai: tail of dmesg from gnode-8342:
```
[3209876543.123] nvme0: I/O 0x1a2 failed, status: media error
[3209876543.456] writeback: backlog prevented by task ephemeral-cleaner
```
maria: immediate plan: 1) cordon affected hosts 2) try graceful restart of cleaner 3) fallback GPU provisioning to us-west 4) enable aggressive ephemeral delete for 30m.
sam: cordoned 6 hosts in us-east1, ran `kill -15` on cleaner (pid 2432) on gnode-8342, cleaner respawned but is stuck again :grimacing:.
kai: tagging @netops — seeing metadata service timeouts from those hosts to 10.0.12.44:8200, looks like RPC latency spike.
mike: (netops) looking now — BGP flap reported near eq-sr01 at 15:40 UTC, some AS paths preferred a longer/unstable hop causing packet loss. rolling a peering reroute now.
maria: mitigation deployed: reduced janitor concurrency to 2 on affected nodes, enabled local KV prefix cache to avoid frequent metadata calls; monitoring disk_used and tempfile_count.
ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0432 (sev3) — assigned to eng-oncall.
sam: cost note — if we shift GPU jobs to other regions for 2h we'll hit ~+$8k in spot premium. ok to proceed? :money_with_wings:
maria: proceed for high-priority queues only; let low-priority backlog. coordinate with scheduler.
kai: will follow up with a postmortem and a patch: janitor should use async metadata calls with timeout backoff to avoid global blocking. also propose autoscaling trigger: preemptive cleanup when scratch usage >85%.
sam: thanks all. updating status page and scheduling a small canary rollout for the cleaner fix to avoid regressions.
